title: Campaign update 1: human motor cortex structure, nine pre-registered papers on BrainGate and monkey Utah-array data (28 November 2026)
abstract: Progress update for the campaign on low-dimensional structure in human motor cortex. Nine papers were published on leaves A2, B1, B2, C1, C2 and D1, each with two internal reviews. Pre-registered results: a decoding-ceiling test was inconclusive, a dimensionality-saturation test failed, and a faster-than-log2 prediction failed on new monkey data (no ceiling within 64-96 electrodes; post hoc, none up to 96-192); spike-band-power tuning similarity after 2 years fell to 14% and 26% of its 1-month value in two humans, and a yield/noise control failed; in one monkey aligned latents passed a similarity test that null surrogates also pass, and an aligned-decoder test was inconclusive; cross-monkey decoder transfer failed; task-free array measures did not reliably predict same-day decoding; channel measures predicted later channel loss, mainly through closeness to the threshold (post hoc); with few calibration trials, more electrodes helped linear decoders more than more sessions, while a small GRU gained from sessions. Several secondary predictions failed; see the papers. Most evidence comes from one monkey or from BrainGate summary tables; reviews are internal. A1 and D2 remain untested; human B2 and C2 wait on the raw BrainGate release.
